requirements.requirement: Identify the physical dual-transit topology between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense), and the private-network hosts node3/node4
requirements.summary: Interface enumeration (ip -br link, ifconfig -a) plus tcpdump/bridge-ID correlation on node1 and node2 established exact NIC-to-network mapping (eth1<->vtnet1 transit A, eth2<->vtnet2 transit B, eth3<->node3 private, vtnet3<->node4 private), directly observed in captured output.

requirements.requirement: Configure redundant-path routing over both transit networks so node1<->node2 have two active paths
requirements.summary: OSPF area 0 configured on VyOS (node1) and via FRR on OPNsense (node2) across both transit subnets 10.10.10.0/30 and 10.10.20.0/30; 'show ip ospf neighbor' shows Full adjacencies over both links and 'show ip route' shows ECMP nexthops via both eth1/eth2 (and vtnet1/vtnet2) to the remote private network, directly observed post-configuration.

requirements.requirement: Carry traffic between node3's and node4's private networks so the two hosts can reach each other
requirements.summary: After adding return-path static routes on node3 and node4, bidirectional pings between 10.10.30.2 (node3) and 10.10.40.2 (node4) succeed with 0% loss, directly observed both before and after the subsequent restart cycle.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate that node3/node4 keep reaching each other when either transit network is taken out of service, across one such transition
requirements.summary: A continuous ping from node3 to node4 was run while transit link A (node1 eth1 / node2 vtnet1) was administratively downed; only a single packet (seq 20) was lost, OSPF neighbor/route state confirmed traffic shifted fully to transit B during the outage, and after transit A was restored OSPF re-adjacenced (Full/DR) and ECMP routing to both paths was re-confirmed — a directly observed healthy-baseline -> disruption -> recovery transition.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task instruction are directly satisfied by observed evidence: the dual-transit topology was correctly mapped, OSPF/ECMP redundant routing was configured and shown operational over both transit links, node3 and node4 achieved bidirectional reachability, and a live transit-link outage plus recovery was directly demonstrated with only a single dropped ping and confirmed OSPF path withdrawal/re-convergence. Independently of the task contract, the executor also ran the provider-wide restart protocol on all four nodes, each showing a pre-restart baseline, a restart acknowledgement (SSH/exec timeouts during the gap), a changed boot identity (VyOS boot_id, OPNsense kern.boottime, RHEL boot_id), and recovered OSPF/routing/ping state afterward — this evidence is coherent and complete for all four nodes. One caveat: node2's before_prepare boot-identity snapshot (kern.boottime ~Jun 15) differs from the 'baseline' boottime captured just before its deliberate restart (~06:01:59 same day as the session), implying node2 underwent an earlier, undocumented boot-identity change sometime between session start and the deliberate restart demonstration — most likely an artifact of first-boot-from-template rather than an executor action, but this is not conclusively established from the trace.
limitations: The apparent earlier, undocumented boot-identity change on node2 (kern.boottime jumping from a Jun 15 value to a Sep 6 06:01:59 value before the deliberate restart test) is not explained in the trace; it may be a template first-boot artifact rather than an executor-caused restart, but this cannot be confirmed from the evidence available.
OPNsense config.xml backup files (.bak/.bak2/.bak3) created during editing are not confirmed removed in the final snapshot, since /conf is outside the captured /tmp inventory.
Command cmd-6262d8c7bc0143aa returned a proxy-timeout error; success was inferred only indirectly from the subsequent command's output rather than a direct return code for that command.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor mutations were tightly scoped to the task: interface down/up flaps on node1/node2/node3/node4 for MAC/bridge-ID topology discovery (cmd-86ee11cd8c684e0a, cmd-67575e2598594ba3, cmd-0eef5e7907c84b62, cmd-bbf54dad2adb4f63, cmd-56c2e77163094c25) were bounded (seconds) and immediately restored, serving a clear discovery prerequisite. tcpdump capture files on node1 were cleaned up implicitly by the later node1 reboot (no cap_*.log residue in after-executor snapshot). One command (cmd-6262d8c7bc0143aa, editing /etc/rc.conf.d/frr and starting frr) hit a 120s proxy timeout but the subsequent command (cmd-b407936554ca419b) confirms it had actually succeeded (frr running) — not a failed mutation, just an unconfirmed-result artifact. Minor unreverted residue: OPNsense config.xml.bak/.bak2/.bak3 backup copies and temporary python helper scripts (addifs.py, addrules.py, setospf.py) were left in /conf and /tmp respectively on node2, though the reboot-triggered /tmp clear on node2 appears to have removed the scripts (not present in after-executor temp-file listing); the config.xml backups likely remain in /conf but are low-risk, standard defensive copies rather than damaging residue. No failed/conflicting services, no weakened security controls, and no destructive or broad mutations were observed.
